findings.reason: the fixture is what makes the guard fire; unless the done-when requires it to reproduce the source that answered present (the aggregate), the first case can be green before the fix and the negative control cannot show the refusal.
findings.text: §14's first case names the fixture as writing "a promotion's per-run ledger file" and nothing else, but the read-back it means to falsify (`_ledger_holds_row`, `reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:2055`) answers from the union of the aggregate *and* the per-run document (`ledger.load(..., use_index=False)`, `reckon/ledger.py:1618-1620`), and the plan's own candidate list names "the aggregate ledger" as a possible source of the incident's present answer. If the fixture populates only the per-run document, the rollback removes it and the *unfixed* read-back answers absent, so the assertion — "the refusal then carries the re-promote wording" — holds before any change: the case is green on unfixed code and measures nothing, and the negative control ("restores the read-back that answered present") then asserts a base state the fixture never produced. If instead the fixture must also carry an aggregate row, the done-when does not say so, and the node has to guess which source makes the control fire.
